practiceProblems.title: Problem (Shoes) - Read the problem statement
practiceProblems.description:
Chef has $N$ friends. \
Chef promised that he would gift a pair of shoes (consisting of one left shoe and one right shoe) to each of his $N$ friends. \
Chef already has $M$ left shoes.

What is the minimum number of extra shoes that Chef will have to buy to ensure that he is able to gift a pair of shoes to each of his $N$ friends? **Check sample test cases below for further clarity**
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Chef has $N$ friends. \
Chef promised that he would gift a pair of shoes (consisting of one left shoe and one right shoe) to each of his $N$ friends. \
Chef already has $M$ left shoes.

What is the minimum number of extra shoes that Chef will have to buy to ensure that he is able to gift a pair of shoes to each of his $N$ friends? **Check sample test cases below for further clarity**
practiceProblems.inputFormat:
- The first line contains a single integer $T$ - the number of test cases. Then the test cases follow.
- The first line of each test case contains two integers $N$ and $M$ - the number of Chef's friends and the number of left shoes Chef has.
practiceProblems.outputFormat: For each test case, output the minimum number of extra shoes that Chef will have to buy to ensure that he is able to get $N$ pairs of shoes.

sampleTestCases.explanation:
**Test Case 1:** Chef initially has $4$ left shoes. He must buy $2$ right shoes to form $2$ pairs of shoes.

**Test Case 2:** Chef initially has no left shoes. He must buy $6$ more left shoes and $6$ more right shoes to form $6$ pairs of shoes.

**Test Case 3:** Chef initially has $3$ left shoes. He must buy $1$ more left shoe and $4$ more right shoes to form $4$ pairs of shoes.

practiceProblems.title: Problem (Shoes) - Observations & Logic
practiceProblems.description:
What do we observe here / what is the logic?
- Whenever $N \leq M$ - i.e. the number of pair of shoes required is less than the number of left shoes available, then Chef needs to buy $N$ right shoes
- When $N \gt M$ - how many shoes does Chef need to buy?
  - Chef already has $M$ left shoes. He will need to buy $(N - M)$ left shoes
  - Chef will need to buy $N$ right shoes
  - Chef will need to buy a total of $(N + N - M)$, i.e. $(2*N - M)$ shoes 

Once the observation / logic is clear, click on 'Next' to proceed.
